questions.subject: science
questions.q: Crops that are sown in the winter season (October to December) and harvested in spring are called:
questions.explanation: Rabi crops such as wheat, gram, peas and mustard are sown in winter and harvested in spring.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is a kharif crop?
questions.explanation: Paddy (rice) is sown at the start of the rainy season, so it is a kharif crop.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Loosening and turning of the soil before sowing seeds is called:
questions.explanation: Tilling (ploughing) loosens the soil so that roots can go deep and soil organisms can mix the soil.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is a manure and not a chemical fertiliser?
questions.explanation: Manure is made from decomposed plant and animal waste, such as compost. Urea and NPK are factory-made fertilisers.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why do farmers grow a leguminous crop such as gram or peas in a field after a cereal crop?
questions.answer: Leguminous plants have Rhizobium bacteria in their root nodules. These bacteria fix nitrogen from the air and add nitrogen compounds to the soil, so the soil becomes richer for the next crop.
keyPoints: Roots of legumes have Rhizobium bacteria
questions.explanation: Crop rotation with legumes restores soil nitrogen naturally.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A farmer has sandy soil, very little water and an orchard of fruit trees. Which method of irrigation would save the most water for her?
options: Flooding the field from a canal
questions.explanation: The drip system delivers water drop by drop at the roots of each plant, so almost none is wasted.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A farmer stores harvested wheat in a sack without drying it properly. What is the most likely result?
options: Moisture lets fungi and pests grow and spoil the grain
The grain slowly turns into manure
The grain becomes richer in nutrients
The grain gets converted into seeds of a new variety
questions.explanation: Damp grain allows moulds, insects and rodents to thrive, so grain must be dried before storage.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why is the excessive use of chemical fertilisers harmful to the environment?
questions.answer: Excess fertilisers reduce soil fertility over time and are washed into ponds and rivers, where they cause pollution and harm water life. They can also contaminate drinking water.
keyPoints: Reduces soil fertility in the long run
Washed into water bodies and pollutes them
questions.explanation: Fertilisers should be used in the right amount, and manure helps maintain soil health.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is a fungus?
questions.explanation: Yeast is a single-celled fungus. Amoeba is a protozoan, Rhizobium is a bacterium and Chlamydomonas is an alga.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Malaria is spread by:
questions.explanation: Malaria is caused by a protozoan Plasmodium carried by the female Anopheles mosquito. Aedes spreads dengue.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Rhizobium bacteria are useful to farmers because they:
options: Fix atmospheric nitrogen in the root nodules of legumes
questions.explanation: Rhizobium lives in root nodules of pulse plants and converts nitrogen of the air into a form plants can use.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Dough used for making bread rises because:
options: Yeast kills bacteria in the flour
Yeast respires and releases bubbles of carbon dioxide
questions.explanation: Yeast respires on the sugar in dough and gives out carbon dioxide, which makes the dough rise.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: How does adding a large amount of salt help in preserving pickles and fish?
questions.answer: Salt removes moisture from the food and from any microorganisms that land on it, so they cannot grow. This keeps the food from spoiling for a long time.
questions.explanation: Common salt is used to preserve meat, fish, pickles and raw mangoes.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A person with influenza, which is caused by a virus, takes an antibiotic. What is true about this treatment?
options: It will not work because antibiotics act against bacteria and not viruses
It will kill the virus within a day
It works better than any other medicine for viruses
It will turn the virus into a harmless bacterium
questions.explanation: Antibiotics are effective only against bacteria. They have no effect on common cold and flu viruses.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In pasteurisation, milk is heated and then chilled quickly. Why is it chilled quickly?
options: To increase the amount of cream
To prevent any surviving microorganisms from multiplying
To add vitamin D to it
questions.explanation: Heating kills most microbes, and rapid chilling stops any survivors from growing.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why should a patient take an antibiotic only on a doctor's advice and complete the full course?
questions.answer: The doctor knows the right type and dose for the infection. If the dose is too small or the course is stopped early, the bacteria may survive, and the medicine may become less effective on them in future. Unnecessary antibiotics can also harm useful bacteria in the body.
keyPoints: Right medicine and dose for the infection
Wrong use makes antibiotics less effective later
questions.explanation: Misuse of antibiotics makes bacteria harder to kill.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following was the first fully synthetic fibre?
questions.explanation: Nylon was the first fully man-made fibre, prepared from coal, water and air.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Rayon, made from wood pulp, is also called:
questions.explanation: Rayon looks like silk but is cheaper and is made from cellulose of wood pulp.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is a thermosetting plastic?
questions.explanation: Bakelite hardens permanently once moulded and cannot be softened again by heating.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Handles of electrical switches are made from Bakelite because it:
options: Is a good conductor of electricity
Is a poor conductor of heat and electricity
questions.explanation: Bakelite is a poor conductor of heat and electricity, so it is safe for switches and handles.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is the difference between thermoplastics and thermosetting plastics? Give one example of each.
questions.answer: Thermoplastics soften on heating and can be reshaped again and again, for example polythene. Thermosetting plastics harden once moulded and cannot be softened by heating, for example Bakelite.
keyPoints: Thermoplastics can be softened and reshaped
Thermosetting plastics cannot be softened again
questions.explanation: The difference is in how they behave on reheating.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why is a layer of Teflon applied on the surface of non-stick frying pans?
options: It is a good conductor so food cooks faster
It is very slippery, so food does not stick to it
It reacts with the food and flavours it
questions.explanation: Teflon is slippery and heat resistant, so food does not stick to the pan.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Plastic bags thrown away in a field remain there for many years. This is because:
options: Plastic dissolves in soil to form humus
Microorganisms cannot break down most plastics, so they are non-biodegradable
questions.explanation: Plastics are non-biodegradable, so they stay in the environment and cause pollution.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why is it not advised to wear clothes made of nylon or polyester while working near a flame in the kitchen?
questions.answer: Synthetic fibres catch fire easily and melt when heated. The molten fibre sticks to the skin and causes severe burns.
keyPoints: Melted fibre sticks to skin and burns
questions.explanation: Cotton clothes are safer near a flame.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which metal is liquid at room temperature?
questions.explanation: Mercury is the only metal that is a liquid at ordinary room temperature.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is a non-metal?
questions.explanation: Sulphur is a brittle, yellow non-metal. The others are metals.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The property of metals by which they can be drawn into wires is called:
questions.explanation: Ductility is the ability to be drawn into thin wires. Malleability is the ability to be beaten into sheets.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Magnesium ribbon reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid and a gas is released. The gas is:
questions.explanation: Metals such as magnesium react with dilute acids to produce hydrogen gas.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Give two reasons why metals are used for making cooking vessels.
questions.answer: Metals are good conductors of heat, so food cooks quickly. They also have high melting points and can be shaped into vessels because they are malleable.
questions.explanation: These properties make metals suitable for utensils.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Carbon dioxide dissolved in water turns blue litmus paper red. What does this show?
options: Carbon dioxide is a basic oxide
Carbon dioxide forms a neutral solution
questions.explanation: Non-metal oxides such as carbon dioxide form acidic solutions in water.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: An iron nail is dipped in blue copper sulphate solution. After some time a brownish coating forms on the nail and the blue colour fades. Why?
options: Copper displaces iron from the solution
More reactive iron displaces copper from the solution
Water in the solution turns into copper
questions.explanation: Iron is more reactive than copper, so it displaces copper, which deposits on the nail.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why are sodium and potassium stored in kerosene oil?
questions.answer: Sodium and potassium are very reactive metals. They react vigorously with oxygen and moisture of the air and can catch fire, so they are kept immersed in kerosene to keep air and water away.
keyPoints: React with oxygen and moisture, may catch fire
Kerosene keeps air and water away
questions.explanation: Storing them in kerosene prevents accidents.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is a fossil fuel?
questions.explanation: Petroleum formed from remains of tiny sea organisms buried for millions of years.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: CNG stands for:
questions.explanation: CNG is natural gas stored under high pressure and used as a fuel for vehicles.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which petroleum product is used for surfacing roads?
questions.explanation: Bitumen is a thick, black residue from refining petroleum and is used to surface roads.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The process of separating the various constituents of petroleum is called:
questions.explanation: Refining separates crude petroleum into petrol, diesel, kerosene and other products.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: How is coke obtained from coal and what is one use of coke?
questions.answer: Coke is obtained by heating coal strongly in the absence of air. It is a tough, porous, black substance that is almost pure carbon, and is used in making steel and in extracting many metals.
keyPoints: Coal heated in absence of air
Used in steel making or extraction of metals
questions.explanation: Coke is a useful product of coal processing.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Coal is called a non-renewable resource because:
options: It cannot be burnt a second time
It is found only in India
It took millions of years to form and cannot be replaced quickly
questions.explanation: Coal forms very slowly from buried plants, so once used it cannot be replenished in a human lifetime.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why is CNG considered a cleaner fuel than petrol or diesel for vehicles?
options: It burns with much less harmful smoke and fewer pollutants
It does not burn at all
It produces no gas on burning
questions.explanation: CNG burns more completely and causes less air pollution.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why should we conserve petroleum and natural gas?
questions.answer: They took millions of years to form and their stocks are limited. Burning them also pollutes the air, so we should use them carefully and look for other sources of energy.
keyPoints: Took millions of years to form
questions.explanation: Saving fuel helps future generations and the environment.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The process of burning a substance in air to give out heat is called:
questions.explanation: Combustion is a chemical process in which a substance burns in oxygen and gives heat.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which zone of a candle flame is the hottest?
questions.explanation: The outermost zone gets plenty of air, burns completely and is the hottest.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following sets of three are necessary for a fire to start and continue?
questions.explanation: A fire needs fuel, oxygen (air) and heat to reach the ignition temperature.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which fire extinguisher is best for a fire caused by electrical equipment?
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide does not conduct electricity and does not damage the equipment, whereas water can conduct electricity.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is meant by ignition temperature? Give one example of how it matters in daily life.
questions.answer: Ignition temperature is the lowest temperature at which a substance catches fire. For example, white phosphorus has a very low ignition temperature, so it is kept under water.
keyPoints: Lowest temperature at which a substance catches fire
Example such as white phosphorus kept under water
questions.explanation: Substances with a low ignition temperature catch fire easily.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why is water not used to put out a fire caused by burning oil?
options: Oil is lighter than water, floats on it and keeps burning
Water reacts with oil to make more fuel
Water is lighter than oil, so it floats away
Water has a very high ignition temperature
questions.explanation: Oil floats on water and continues to burn, so the fire can even spread.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A burning candle is covered with an upside-down glass jar and it goes out after some time. The reason is that:
options: The glass makes the wax cold
The oxygen inside the jar is used up
The jar contains too much oxygen
questions.explanation: With no fresh air coming in, oxygen is used up and burning stops.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why does a paper cup holding water not catch fire when it is heated over a flame?
questions.answer: The water absorbs the heat from the paper, so the paper stays below its ignition temperature and does not burn.
keyPoints: Paper stays below its ignition temperature
So it does not catch fire
questions.explanation: Water carries away the heat quickly.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The record of endangered species of plants and animals is kept in the:
questions.explanation: The Red Data Book lists species that are endangered or threatened.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Deforestation means:
options: Clearing of forests on a large scale
questions.explanation: Deforestation is the large-scale cutting down of trees and clearing of forest land.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A species that is found only in a particular area and nowhere else is called:
questions.explanation: Endemic species are native to and found only in one specific region.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is a biosphere reserve? Name one biosphere reserve in India.
questions.answer: A biosphere reserve is a large protected area set aside to conserve the biodiversity of its plants and animals, and often the way of life of the people living there. One example is the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve.
keyPoints: Conserves plants, animals and their habitat
questions.explanation: Biosphere reserves protect whole ecosystems.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Reforestation means:
options: Restocking destroyed forests by planting trees
questions.explanation: Reforestation is planting trees to replace forests that have been cut or destroyed.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A highway built through a forest area is most likely to harm wild animals because:
options: It breaks up their habitat and blocks their movement
It increases the number of trees
questions.explanation: Roads divide habitats, reduce space and make crossing dangerous for animals.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Explain how deforestation can lead to soil erosion and rise in temperature.
questions.answer: Roots of trees bind the soil, so without trees the soil is easily washed or blown away. Fewer trees also absorb less carbon dioxide and give less shade and rain, so the surroundings become hotter and drier.
keyPoints: Roots hold soil, so soil erodes
Less rain and shade, so more heat
questions.explanation: Trees protect soil and help keep the climate balanced.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The basic structural and functional unit of life is the:
questions.explanation: All living things are made of cells, which carry out the activities of life.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Who first observed and named cells while looking at a thin slice of cork?
questions.explanation: Robert Hooke saw box-like compartments in cork under a microscope and called them cells.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The part of a cell that contains the chromosomes carrying genes is the:
questions.explanation: The nucleus holds the chromosomes and controls the activities of the cell.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Write two differences between a plant cell and an animal cell.
questions.answer: A plant cell has a cell wall outside the cell membrane, but an animal cell does not. A plant cell has chloroplasts and usually a large central vacuole, while an animal cell has no chloroplasts and only small vacuoles.
keyPoints: Cell wall present only in plant cells
Plant cells have a large vacuole
questions.explanation: These features suit the way plants and animals live.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The organelle in which photosynthesis takes place is the:
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll, which traps sunlight for photosynthesis.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following cells would you expect to have the most chloroplasts?
options: A cell of a green leaf
A root cell inside the soil
A cell of the onion bulb
questions.explanation: Leaf cells carry out photosynthesis in light, so they contain many chloroplasts.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why do plant cells have a cell wall while animal cells do not need one?
questions.answer: The cell wall gives plant cells shape, strength and protection. Plants have no skeleton, so the rigid wall helps them stay upright, while animals get support from skeletons and muscles.
keyPoints: Cell wall gives shape and strength
Animals are supported by other body parts
questions.explanation: The wall is made of cellulose and supports the plant body.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The fusion of a male gamete and a female gamete is called:
questions.explanation: Fertilisation is the joining of a sperm and an egg to form a zygote.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The male gamete is called the:
questions.explanation: Sperms are produced in the testes and are male gametes.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following reproduces by budding?
questions.explanation: A Hydra forms a bud on its body that grows into a new individual. Amoeba divides by binary fission.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Differentiate between internal and external fertilisation. Give one example of each.
questions.answer: In internal fertilisation the sperm and egg join inside the body of the female, for example in humans or hens. In external fertilisation they join outside the body, in water, for example in frogs and fish.
keyPoints: External: outside body, usually in water
Examples such as hen and frog
questions.explanation: The place of fertilisation differs.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is a viviparous animal?
questions.explanation: Viviparous animals give birth to young ones instead of laying eggs.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A frog lays hundreds of eggs but a hen lays only a few. Which reason explains this best?
options: Frog eggs are fertilised and develop in open water, where many eggs are eaten or lost, so more eggs improve survival chances
Hens do not need eggs to reproduce
Frog eggs are fertilised inside the female
questions.explanation: External fertilisation in water has many risks, so large numbers of eggs help some young survive.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Describe the changes in the life of a frog from egg to adult.
questions.answer: The fertilised egg develops into a tadpole that has a tail and gills and lives in water. The tadpole slowly grows legs, loses the tail and gills and develops lungs, becoming an adult frog. This change in form is called metamorphosis.
keyPoints: Egg develops into tadpole with gills and tail
questions.explanation: Metamorphosis is a major change of body form.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The period of life roughly between the ages of 11 and 19 years is called:
questions.explanation: Adolescence is the stage of growth between childhood and adulthood.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The male sex hormone produced by the testes is:
questions.explanation: Testosterone produced by the testes brings changes in boys at puberty.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The gland that controls the working of other endocrine glands and is often called the master gland is the:
questions.explanation: The pituitary gland secretes hormones that control other glands.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is the Adam's apple and why does it become visible in adolescent boys?
questions.answer: The Adam's apple is the visible bulge at the front of the neck. During adolescence the voice box (larynx) grows larger in boys, so it sticks out and the voice becomes deeper.
keyPoints: It is the enlarged voice box (larynx)
Seen as a bulge in the neck
questions.explanation: Growth of the larynx changes the voice.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Lack of iodine in the diet can cause a swelling of the neck called:
questions.explanation: The thyroid gland needs iodine to make thyroxine, and its shortage causes goitre.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The sex of a human baby is decided by:
options: The X chromosome in the mother's egg
The X or Y chromosome carried by the father's sperm
The hormones of both parents at birth
questions.explanation: Every egg carries an X chromosome. A sperm with X gives a girl and a sperm with Y gives a boy.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why do adolescents need a balanced diet and regular exercise?
questions.answer: Adolescents grow fast and need more proteins, vitamins and minerals for their growing body. Regular exercise keeps the body fit and healthy and helps the mind.
keyPoints: Balanced diet gives proteins, vitamins and minerals
questions.explanation: Good habits during this stage support health later in life.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The SI unit of force is the:
questions.explanation: Force is measured in newtons (N).

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Force acting per unit area is called:
questions.explanation: Pressure equals force divided by the area on which it acts.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The force of friction always acts:
options: In the direction opposite to the motion
In the direction of the motion
At right angles to the surface only
questions.explanation: Friction opposes the relative motion between two surfaces in contact.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why are the soles of sports shoes made with grooves or a rough pattern?
questions.answer: Grooves increase friction between the shoe and the ground, so the player can grip the ground well and does not slip.
questions.explanation: More friction gives better grip.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is a non-contact force?
questions.explanation: Gravity acts on objects without touching them.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A sharp knife cuts a vegetable more easily than a blunt knife because:
options: With a smaller area of the edge, the same force gives a greater pressure
questions.explanation: Pressure is force divided by area, so a thin edge produces a large pressure.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A camel can walk easily on soft sand without sinking. Explain why.
questions.answer: A camel has broad, flat feet. The broad area spreads its weight over a larger area, so the pressure on the sand is smaller and the feet do not sink.
questions.explanation: Pressure decreases as the area increases.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Sound is produced when an object:
questions.explanation: All sounds are produced by vibrating objects.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The unit in which frequency is measured is:
questions.explanation: Frequency is the number of vibrations per second and is measured in hertz (Hz).

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The loudness of a sound depends on the:
questions.explanation: A larger amplitude of vibration gives a louder sound.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why can sound not travel through a vacuum?
questions.answer: Sound needs a material medium such as air, water or a solid to travel. A vacuum has no particles that can vibrate and pass the sound on.
questions.explanation: Sound travels by making particles of a medium vibrate.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The range of frequencies audible to a normal human ear is about:
questions.explanation: Humans can hear sounds from about 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A girl's voice is usually thinner (higher pitched) than that of a grown man. The reason is:
options: Lower amplitude of her vocal cords
Her vocal cords vibrate at a lower frequency
Her vocal cords vibrate at a higher frequency
questions.explanation: Higher frequency of vibration gives a higher pitch.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Suggest three ways in which noise pollution in a city can be reduced.
questions.answer: Noise can be reduced by switching off vehicle horns and engines when not needed, keeping the volume of music and TV low, and planting trees along roads. Using silencers on machines also helps.
questions.explanation: Noise above comfortable levels harms hearing and health.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following liquids conducts electricity?
questions.explanation: Lemon juice contains acid, so it has ions and conducts electricity. Distilled water, oil and sugar solution do not.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Depositing a layer of a metal on another object using electric current is called:
questions.explanation: Electroplating uses electric current to coat an object with a thin layer of metal.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: When electric current passes through a conducting solution, it can cause:
questions.explanation: Current through a conducting solution can produce bubbles, colour changes or metal deposits, which are chemical effects.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: How can you test whether a liquid is a good conductor of electricity?
questions.answer: Make a tester using a cell, a bulb or LED and two wires with free ends. Dip the free ends in the liquid. If the bulb glows or the LED lights up, the liquid conducts electricity.
keyPoints: Use a cell, bulb or LED and wires
Dip the wire ends in the liquid
questions.explanation: The tester completes the circuit through the liquid.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In electroplating, the object to be plated is connected to:
options: The negative terminal of the battery
The positive terminal of the battery
questions.explanation: The article to be plated is the cathode, connected to the negative terminal.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Chromium plating is done on car parts and bicycle handlebars because chromium:
options: Is shiny, hard and does not corrode easily
questions.explanation: A chromium coat gives a bright finish and protects the metal from rusting.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why should we not touch an electrical switch with wet hands?
questions.answer: Ordinary water contains dissolved salts, so it conducts electricity. Wet hands can let current pass through the body and cause an electric shock.
keyPoints: Ordinary water contains salts and conducts
questions.explanation: Keep hands dry around electrical appliances.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: According to the law of reflection, the angle of incidence is equal to the:
questions.explanation: The angle of incidence always equals the angle of reflection.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The image formed by a plane mirror is:
options: Virtual and upright, of the same size as the object
questions.explanation: A plane mirror gives a virtual, erect image the same size as the object.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which is the safest place to be during a thunderstorm?
questions.explanation: A closed building protects you from lightning, while tall trees and open ground are dangerous.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Name the instrument used to record earthquake waves and the scale on which the strength of an earthquake is measured.
questions.answer: A seismograph records earthquake waves. The strength (magnitude) of an earthquake is measured on the Richter scale.
questions.explanation: Earthquakes are measured by magnitude.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The splitting of white light into its seven colours is called:
questions.explanation: Dispersion occurs when a prism or raindrops split white light into a spectrum.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The word AMBULANCE is written laterally inverted on the front of the vehicle. This is done so that:
options: The word can be read correctly in the rear-view mirror of the car ahead
The word is hidden from the driver
questions.explanation: A mirror reverses left and right, so inverted writing reads correctly in a mirror.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: During a thunderstorm we see lightning first and hear thunder later. Why?
questions.answer: Light travels much faster than sound. The flash of lightning reaches our eyes almost instantly, while the sound of thunder takes longer to reach our ears.
keyPoints: Light is much faster than sound
Flash is seen almost at once
questions.explanation: Speed of light is about a million times that of sound in air.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The process of separating the lighter husk (chaff) from the grain using the wind is called:
questions.explanation: In winnowing, grain and chaff are poured from a height, and the wind blows the lighter chaff away.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Cutting a mature crop from the field is called:
questions.explanation: Harvesting is the cutting of the mature crop, usually with a sickle or a combine harvester.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which tool is used to sow seeds at a uniform distance and depth in the soil?
questions.explanation: A seed drill is a tractor-driven tool that drops seeds evenly and covers them with soil.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is weeding and why is it necessary in a crop field?
questions.answer: Weeding is the removal of unwanted plants (weeds) that grow along with the crop. Weeds compete with the crop for water, nutrients, light and space, so removing them helps the crop grow well.
keyPoints: Weeds compete for water, nutrients and light
questions.explanation: Weeds can be removed by hand, with a trowel or with weedicides.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is an advantage of manure over a chemical fertiliser?
options: It supplies nutrients faster and in a larger quantity
It contains more nutrients for each kilogram
It improves the texture of the soil and its ability to hold water by adding humus
It is easier to carry long distances
questions.explanation: Manure adds humus, which makes the soil porous and helps it retain water, unlike a fertiliser.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: When seeds are put in water, damaged seeds float on the surface. This is because damaged seeds are:
questions.explanation: Damaged or hollow seeds are lighter and float, so good seeds can be selected as they sink.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why are dried neem leaves often kept with stored grain in homes?
questions.answer: Neem leaves keep insects and pests away. This helps to protect the stored grains from damage and spoilage.
keyPoints: Neem leaves repel insects and pests
questions.explanation: Neem leaves are a traditional way of protecting stored grain.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following diseases is caused by a virus?
questions.explanation: The common cold is caused by a virus. Typhoid, cholera and tuberculosis are caused by bacteria.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is the smallest?
questions.explanation: Viruses are much smaller than bacteria and can only be seen with a powerful microscope.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The conversion of sugar into alcohol by yeast is called:
questions.explanation: Fermentation by yeast turns sugar into alcohol and carbon dioxide.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is a vaccine and how does it protect us from disease?
questions.answer: A vaccine contains weakened or dead disease-causing microbes. When it is given, the body makes antibodies against them, so if the real microbe attacks later, the body can fight it quickly.
questions.explanation: Vaccines prevent diseases such as polio and measles.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Green fuzzy patches appear on a piece of bread kept in a warm and damp cupboard. They are most likely due to:
options: Dust that has settled on the bread
Fungal spores growing in warm, moist conditions
questions.explanation: Fungal spores in the air grow on bread that is moist and warm and form a fuzzy mould.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which statement best explains how some bacteria help to keep the environment clean?
options: They make dead plants and animals last longer
They decompose dead plants and animals into simple substances
questions.explanation: Decomposer bacteria and fungi break down dead matter and return nutrients to the soil.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: How can a housefly spread diseases like cholera? Suggest one precaution.
questions.answer: Houseflies sit on garbage and animal waste and pick up disease-causing microbes on their legs and bodies. When they sit on uncovered food they pass these microbes on. We should keep food covered and keep the surroundings clean.
keyPoints: Cover food and keep surroundings clean
questions.explanation: Flies are carriers of disease.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is a natural fibre?
questions.explanation: Cotton comes from the cotton plant. Nylon, acrylic and polyester are synthetic.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which synthetic fibre is often called artificial wool?
questions.explanation: Acrylic looks like wool and is used for sweaters, shawls and blankets.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Terylene is a kind of:
questions.explanation: Terylene is a well-known polyester, which is crease-resistant and easy to wash.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Write any two properties of plastics that make them useful.
questions.answer: Plastics are light, strong and durable, and they are poor conductors of heat and electricity. They can also be moulded easily into many shapes and do not rust.
keyPoints: Poor conductors of heat and electricity
questions.explanation: Such properties explain the wide use of plastics.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A mountaineer needs a rope that is strong, light and does not rot in water. Which fibre is the best choice?
questions.explanation: Nylon is very strong, light, elastic and does not absorb much water, so it is used for ropes.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Strong chemicals are often stored in plastic containers rather than metal ones because plastics:
options: Are generally non-reactive with many chemicals
questions.explanation: Most plastics do not react with acids or other chemicals, so they do not get corroded.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Suggest three ways in which pollution from plastic can be reduced.
questions.answer: We can reduce the use of plastic bags by carrying cloth or jute bags, reuse plastic containers where safe, and send used plastic to be recycled. We should not throw plastic carelessly or burn it.
questions.explanation: Plastic is non-biodegradable, so its waste must be managed.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following metals is soft enough to be cut with a knife?
questions.explanation: Sodium is a very soft metal and can be cut with a knife.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following non-metals is a good conductor of electricity?
questions.explanation: Graphite, a form of carbon, is an exception among non-metals and conducts electricity.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Metals are said to be sonorous. This means they:
options: Can be cut with a knife
Produce a ringing sound when struck
questions.explanation: Sonorous metals ring when hit, which is why school bells are made of metal.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A magnesium ribbon is burnt in air and the white ash is dissolved in water. What is the effect of this solution on red litmus paper, and why?
questions.answer: The ash is magnesium oxide, a metal oxide, and it dissolves in water to form a basic solution. It turns red litmus paper blue.
questions.explanation: Metal oxides are generally basic in nature.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Gold and silver are used to make jewellery because they:
options: Are lustrous and do not corrode easily
questions.explanation: Gold and silver are shiny, malleable and keep their lustre for a long time.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: For an iron nail to rust, which of the following are necessary?
questions.explanation: Iron rusts in the presence of both air (oxygen) and water.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why are electric wires made of metal but covered with plastic?
questions.answer: The metal is a good conductor, so it carries electric current easily. Plastic is a poor conductor (an insulator), so it prevents shocks and short circuits.
questions.explanation: The wire and its cover do different jobs.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The main constituent of natural gas is:
questions.explanation: Natural gas is mainly methane, which is also the main constituent of CNG.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Petroleum is also commonly called:
questions.explanation: Petroleum is called black gold because of its dark colour and great value.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following petroleum products is commonly used as fuel for domestic stoves and lamps?
questions.explanation: Kerosene is used as a fuel for stoves and lamps.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Name any four products obtained from petroleum and give one use of each.
questions.answer: Petrol is used as a fuel in cars, diesel in trucks and buses, kerosene in stoves, and LPG for cooking. Paraffin wax is used for candles, lubricating oil in machines and bitumen for roads.
questions.explanation: Refining gives many useful products.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which statement correctly differentiates coal from petroleum?
options: Coal formed from buried sea organisms and petroleum from forests
Coal formed from buried plants of ancient forests and petroleum from tiny sea organisms
Both formed in a few years
questions.explanation: Coal formed from plants buried in swamps, while petroleum formed from dead sea organisms.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Burning coal in factories can lead to acid rain because:
options: Burning coal releases sulphur dioxide, which dissolves in rainwater
questions.explanation: Sulphur dioxide from burning coal forms acids in rainwater and damages buildings and plants.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Explain in brief how petroleum was formed.
questions.answer: Millions of years ago, tiny sea plants and animals died and sank to the sea floor. They were covered by layers of sand and clay, and with heat and pressure over a very long time they changed into petroleum and natural gas.
keyPoints: Dead sea organisms settled on sea floor
Heat and pressure over millions of years
questions.explanation: Petroleum is a fossil fuel.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which fuel is used in rockets because of its very high calorific value?
questions.explanation: Hydrogen has the highest calorific value among common fuels and is used as rocket fuel.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is a non-combustible substance?
questions.explanation: Glass does not burn, so it is non-combustible.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The calorific value of a fuel is expressed in:
questions.explanation: Calorific value is the heat produced on complete burning of 1 kg of fuel, in kilojoules per kg.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is spontaneous combustion? Give an example.
questions.answer: It is the type of combustion in which a substance suddenly catches fire on its own without any external flame or heat. White phosphorus catching fire in air at room temperature is an example.
questions.explanation: Such substances have a very low ignition temperature.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A blanket is thrown over a person whose clothes have caught fire because it:
options: Cuts off the supply of air and cools the fire
questions.explanation: Covering stops fresh air from reaching the burning cloth, so the fire goes out.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The flame of a gas stove burns blue, whereas a candle flame is yellow. The blue flame indicates:
questions.explanation: A blue flame means plenty of air and complete burning. A yellow flame has unburnt carbon particles.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why is it dangerous to burn coal in a closed room?
questions.answer: In a closed room the supply of oxygen is limited, so the coal undergoes incomplete combustion and gives out carbon monoxide, a poisonous gas. It can make people unconscious and can even kill them.
questions.explanation: Rooms with burning fuel should be well ventilated.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A protected area where wild animals are safe from hunting is called a:
questions.explanation: In a sanctuary, animals are protected from hunting and poaching.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Species that no longer exist on Earth are called:
questions.explanation: Extinct species have disappeared completely.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The term fauna refers to:
questions.explanation: Flora is plant life and fauna is animal life of a region.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: One of the main reasons for deforestation is:
options: Clearing land for farming, housing and industries
questions.explanation: Forests are cut for agriculture, buildings, roads and wood.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is an endangered species? Give one example.
questions.answer: An endangered species is a species of plant or animal whose numbers have fallen so low that it is in danger of becoming extinct. The tiger is an example.
questions.explanation: Endangered species need special protection.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Forests help to reduce floods because:
options: Roots of trees hold the soil and slow down the flow of rainwater
Forests increase the number of rivers
questions.explanation: Roots bind soil and absorb water, so rainwater runs off slowly.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following actions would help the most to save a species from extinction?
options: Cutting the forest to build farms
Moving all its animals to one zoo
Banning hunting and protecting its habitat
questions.explanation: Protecting the habitat and stopping poaching let the population recover.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why do some birds travel long distances to other regions every year?
questions.answer: They migrate to escape harsh weather such as extreme cold, to find food, or to breed in a suitable place. Many return when the climate is favourable again.
questions.explanation: Migration helps birds survive and raise young.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The jelly-like substance that fills the cell and lies between the cell membrane and the nucleus is the:
questions.explanation: Cytoplasm is the jelly-like fluid in which organelles are found.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which organelle is known as the powerhouse of the cell?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria release energy from food during respiration.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The part of the cell that controls the movement of substances in and out of the cell is the:
questions.explanation: The cell membrane is selectively permeable and lets only some substances pass.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is a unicellular organism?
questions.explanation: Amoeba is made of a single cell.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is the difference between unicellular and multicellular organisms? Give one example of each.
questions.answer: Unicellular organisms consist of a single cell that does all life functions, for example Amoeba. Multicellular organisms are made of many cells that are specialised for different functions, for example humans.
keyPoints: Examples such as Amoeba and humans
questions.explanation: Cells in multicellular organisms divide the work.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Nerve cells are long and branched. What is the most suitable reason?
options: Their shape helps them carry messages over long distances in the body
To make the body look attractive
questions.explanation: The shape of a cell suits its function. Nerve cells carry messages.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Under a microscope, onion peel cells appear as regular, closely packed rectangles with thick outlines. The thick outline is due to the:
questions.explanation: Plant cells have a rigid cell wall that gives them a regular shape.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why are cells called the building blocks of life?
questions.answer: Every living organism is made of one or more cells, just as a building is made of bricks. Cells group to form tissues, organs and organ systems, and each cell carries out life processes.
keyPoints: All organisms are made of cells
questions.explanation: The cell is the basic unit of structure and function.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The female gametes (eggs) are produced in the:
questions.explanation: Ovaries produce the female gametes called ova.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In a human female, fertilisation takes place in the:
questions.explanation: Sperm meets the egg in the oviduct (fallopian tube), forming the zygote.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The developing human baby grows inside the:
questions.explanation: The zygote becomes an embryo and then a foetus inside the uterus.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In Amoeba, binary fission means that:
options: The cell splits into two daughter cells
A bud grows on its body
The cell joins with another cell
questions.explanation: In binary fission one parent cell divides to form two new organisms.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is cloning? Name the first mammal cloned.
questions.answer: Cloning is the production of an exact copy of an organism that has the same genes as the original. The first mammal cloned successfully was a sheep named Dolly.
questions.explanation: Cloning produces an organism genetically identical to its parent.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In the technique called IVF, the egg and sperm are made to join:
options: In a dish in the laboratory, and the embryo is then placed in the uterus
questions.explanation: In IVF fertilisation takes place outside the body, and the early embryo is then placed in the uterus.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: An unfertilised hen's egg bought from a shop will not hatch into a chick because:
options: There was no fusion of a sperm and an egg, so no zygote formed
It is kept in a cold room only
questions.explanation: A chick develops only from a zygote, which forms after fertilisation.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Frogs lay eggs in water, but hens lay eggs with a hard shell. Give a reason for each.
questions.answer: Frog eggs are fertilised outside the body and covered with jelly, and they need water to develop. A hen's egg is fertilised inside and has a hard shell that protects the developing chick on land.
keyPoints: Frog eggs need water and are covered by jelly
Hen's egg has a hard protective shell
questions.explanation: The egg structure suits the habitat.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The changes that occur at puberty are controlled by chemicals called:
questions.explanation: Hormones released by endocrine glands control growth and changes at puberty.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The female sex hormone oestrogen is produced by the:
questions.explanation: Ovaries produce oestrogen, which brings about changes in girls.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The menstrual cycle in a woman repeats about once every:
questions.explanation: A menstrual cycle usually lasts about 28 to 30 days.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is a secondary sexual character?
options: Growth of a beard in boys
questions.explanation: Growth of a beard in boys is a secondary sexual character that appears at puberty.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What are hormones? Name two endocrine glands.
questions.answer: Hormones are chemical substances produced by endocrine glands that are carried by the blood to other parts of the body to control their working. Two endocrine glands are the pituitary gland and the thyroid gland.
keyPoints: Two glands such as pituitary and thyroid
questions.explanation: Endocrine glands have no ducts and release hormones directly into blood.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A person has too much sugar in the blood because the pancreas does not make enough insulin. The disease is:
questions.explanation: Insulin controls the level of sugar in blood, and its shortage causes diabetes.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: When a person is frightened, the adrenal glands release adrenaline. What is the effect?
options: It increases the heart rate and prepares the body to face the situation
It stops the heart for a moment
questions.explanation: Adrenaline speeds up the heartbeat and breathing and prepares the body for action.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why are hormones called chemical messengers?
questions.answer: Hormones are chemicals made in one part of the body, the endocrine gland, and carried by blood to another part, where they bring about a response. In this way they carry a message from one part to another.
questions.explanation: They coordinate body functions.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is a contact force?
questions.explanation: Muscular force needs the body to touch the object.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A force can change:
options: The speed, direction or shape of an object
questions.explanation: A force can change the state of motion or shape of an object.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which type of friction is the least?
questions.explanation: Rolling friction is smaller than sliding or static friction, which is why wheels are used.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Gas exerts pressure on the walls of its container because:
options: Gas particles keep colliding with the walls
questions.explanation: Moving gas particles strike the walls and exert a force on them.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: State two ways of reducing friction.
questions.answer: Friction can be reduced by using lubricants such as oil or grease between moving parts, and by using ball bearings or wheels instead of sliding. Making surfaces smoother also reduces friction.
questions.explanation: Reducing friction saves energy and prevents wear.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Pressure in water increases as we go deeper because:
options: There is more weight of water above
Air is heavier at the bottom
questions.explanation: A deeper point has more water above it, so the pressure is greater.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A heavy box is hard to start moving but easier to keep moving. The reason is that:
options: The box gets lighter after moving
The friction before motion starts is greater than sliding friction
The floor becomes smooth by itself
questions.explanation: Static friction, which acts before motion, is greater than sliding friction.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why is the wall of a dam built thicker at the bottom than at the top?
questions.answer: The pressure of water increases with depth, so the bottom of the dam has to bear more pressure. A thicker wall at the bottom makes the dam strong enough to withstand this.
questions.explanation: Liquid pressure depends on depth.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The number of vibrations of an object in one second is called its:
questions.explanation: Frequency is the number of oscillations per second.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The shrillness (pitch) of a sound depends on its:
questions.explanation: Higher frequency gives a shriller sound.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Loudness of sound is measured in:
questions.explanation: The unit of loudness is the decibel (dB).

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Among air, vacuum, steel and water vapour, sound travels fastest through:
questions.explanation: Sound travels faster in solids than in gases, and cannot travel in a vacuum.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: How is sound produced by the human voice box?
questions.answer: The voice box (larynx) contains two vocal cords stretched across it. When air from the lungs passes through, the vocal cords vibrate and produce sound.
questions.explanation: The tightness of the cords changes the pitch.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Two astronauts walking on the Moon cannot talk to each other directly without radios because:
options: There is no air on the Moon, so sound cannot travel
questions.explanation: The Moon has no air, and sound needs a medium.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Sound A has a frequency of 500 Hz and a small amplitude. Sound B has a frequency of 200 Hz and a large amplitude. Which statement is correct?
options: A is louder and has a lower pitch
A is louder and has a higher pitch
B has the higher pitch and is softer
A has the higher pitch and is softer
questions.explanation: Higher frequency means higher pitch. Smaller amplitude means a softer sound.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A rubber band is stretched and plucked. Why does its sound become shriller when it is stretched more tightly?
questions.answer: A tighter rubber band vibrates faster, so its frequency becomes higher. A higher frequency gives a higher pitch, or shriller sound.
questions.explanation: Pitch depends on the frequency of vibration.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is an insulator of electricity?
questions.explanation: Rubber does not allow current to pass through it.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is a chemical effect of electric current?
options: Formation of gas bubbles at the electrodes
questions.explanation: Gas bubbles at the electrodes show that a chemical change is taking place.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: An LED in a tester glows even when a bulb does not glow, because:
options: An LED works with very small currents
questions.explanation: LEDs glow with a very small current, so they can detect weak conduction.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What happens when electric current is passed through water to which a few drops of acid have been added?
questions.answer: The water breaks down and bubbles of gas form at the electrodes. The gases produced are hydrogen and oxygen.
questions.explanation: This is a chemical effect of current.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: To electroplate a layer of copper on an iron key, the other electrode (the one connected to the positive terminal) should be:
questions.explanation: The copper plate dissolves in the solution and supplies copper that is deposited on the key.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Food cans are made of iron coated with tin. Why?
options: Tin is a poor conductor of sound
Tin is less reactive than iron, so it protects the iron and does not spoil the food
questions.explanation: A coat of tin keeps iron from rusting and does not react readily with food.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why are cheaper metal ornaments sometimes coated with gold or silver by electroplating?
questions.answer: Electroplating gives them the shiny look of the costly metal while using only a thin layer, so they cost less. The coating also protects the cheaper metal from corrosion.
keyPoints: Gives shiny look of costly metal
Only a thin layer needed, so cheaper
questions.explanation: A thin layer of a costly metal is enough for the appearance.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Lightning is caused by:
options: Discharge of electric charges between clouds, or between clouds and the ground
questions.explanation: Lightning is a huge electric spark when charges flow between clouds or to the ground.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Earthquakes are caused by:
options: Disturbance deep inside the Earth's crust
questions.explanation: Earthquakes are caused by movements of the plates of the Earth's crust.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Electric charges are of:
questions.explanation: The two kinds of charge are positive and negative.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: State the rule of attraction and repulsion between electric charges.
questions.answer: Like charges repel each other and unlike charges attract each other.
questions.explanation: This is the basic law of static electricity.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A lightning conductor on a tall building protects it because it:
options: Provides a safe path for the charge to flow to the ground
questions.explanation: Lightning conductors carry the electric charge safely to the ground.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A rainbow is formed because:
options: Water droplets in the air disperse sunlight into its colours
questions.explanation: Raindrops act like tiny prisms, so sunlight is split into seven colours.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Write three precautions to take during an earthquake if you are indoors.
questions.answer: Take shelter under a strong table or desk, stay away from windows, glass and heavy objects that may fall, and protect your head. After the shaking stops, go to an open space calmly.
keyPoints: Stay away from windows and heavy objects
Move to an open area after shaking stops
questions.explanation: Preparedness reduces injuries during earthquakes.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is a cereal crop?
questions.explanation: Wheat is a cereal. Gram is a pulse, and soybean and groundnut are oilseeds.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is a pulse?
questions.explanation: Lentil (masur) is a pulse. Rice, maize and jowar are cereals.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A hoe is a farm tool used for:
options: Removing weeds and loosening the soil
questions.explanation: A hoe is a long rod with a bent, broad, sharp plate that is used to remove weeds and loosen soil.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A combine harvester is a machine that:
options: Harvests the crop and also separates the grain from the husk
questions.explanation: A combine harvester cuts the crop, threshes it and separates the grain in one operation.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is irrigation, and why do crops need it?
questions.answer: Irrigation is the supply of water to crops at regular intervals. Plants need water to absorb nutrients from the soil, and water is also needed for germination, growth and to protect crops from frost and hot air currents.
keyPoints: Supply of water to crops at intervals
questions.explanation: The timing and amount of irrigation differ for each crop.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: If the same crop is grown in the same field year after year, the soil becomes poor because:
options: The same crop takes up the same nutrients from the soil again and again
questions.explanation: Repeatedly growing one crop depletes particular nutrients, so farmers rotate different crops.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A farmer is about to spray a weedicide in the field. Which precaution is most important?
options: Wear a protective cover over the mouth and nose, and wash hands afterwards
Spray when the wind blows toward him
Taste the liquid to check strength
Spray without any cover to save time
questions.explanation: Weedicides are poisonous chemicals, so the farmer must protect his skin and lungs.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why is the soil ploughed and broken into fine pieces before sowing? How do earthworms help?
questions.answer: Loose soil lets the roots go deep, gets more air and lets roots breathe, and brings nutrient-rich soil to the top. Earthworms and microbes in the soil help to turn and mix the soil and add humus, so the soil stays fertile.
keyPoints: Loose soil helps roots penetrate and breathe
Earthworms and microbes turn the soil and add humus
questions.explanation: Soil preparation helps the crop to establish itself.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Curd is formed from milk by the action of:
questions.explanation: Lactobacillus bacteria turn milk into curd.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Penicillin, the first antibiotic, was discovered by:
questions.explanation: Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin from the Penicillium mould.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Edward Jenner developed the first vaccine against:
questions.explanation: Jenner developed the smallpox vaccine.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following diseases can spread through contaminated drinking water?
questions.explanation: Cholera, typhoid and hepatitis A spread through contaminated water.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Explain how curd is made at home from milk.
questions.answer: A little curd, which contains Lactobacillus bacteria, is added to warm milk and left undisturbed for some hours. The bacteria multiply and change the milk into curd.
keyPoints: Add a little curd to warm milk
questions.explanation: The starter curd supplies the bacteria.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why is it advised to boil drinking water in places where the water supply may be unsafe?
questions.explanation: Heat kills most microbes in water that could otherwise cause disease.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Food is stored in a refrigerator because:
options: Low temperature slows the growth of microorganisms
The refrigerator kills all microbes inside
questions.explanation: Cold slows down the growth of microorganisms, so food keeps longer.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Distinguish between a vaccine and an antibiotic.
questions.answer: A vaccine is given before infection to prepare the body to fight a disease by making antibodies, so it prevents illness. An antibiotic is a medicine given to kill or stop bacteria after a person is infected.
keyPoints: Vaccine prevents disease by making antibodies
questions.explanation: One prevents, the other cures bacterial infections.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Fibres obtained from plants and animals, such as cotton, wool and silk, are called:
questions.explanation: Natural fibres come from plant or animal sources.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Polythene is commonly used to make:
questions.explanation: Polythene is a light, flexible thermoplastic used for bags and packaging.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which synthetic fibre is prepared by chemical treatment of wood pulp?
questions.explanation: Rayon is made from the cellulose of wood pulp.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A polymer is:
options: A small single unit of matter
A large molecule made of many small units joined together
questions.explanation: Polymers are made by joining a large number of small units called monomers.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What do biodegradable and non-biodegradable mean? Give one example of each.
questions.answer: Biodegradable materials can be broken down by microorganisms into simple substances, for example vegetable waste. Non-biodegradable materials cannot be broken down in this way, for example plastic bags.
questions.explanation: Plastics stay in the environment for a long time.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Melamine is used to make kitchenware and fire-resistant fabrics because it:
options: Is a good conductor of heat
Resists heat and does not catch fire easily
questions.explanation: Melamine is a thermosetting plastic that resists fire and heat.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Clothes made of synthetic fibres dry faster than cotton clothes because synthetic fibres:
options: Are heated by the Sun more
questions.explanation: Synthetic fibres absorb little water, so they dry quickly.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In hot, humid summers, cotton clothes are more comfortable than polyester clothes. Why?
questions.answer: Cotton absorbs sweat and lets it evaporate, which cools the body. Polyester absorbs very little water, so sweat stays on the skin and the person feels hot and sticky.
questions.explanation: Absorbency decides comfort in hot weather.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following non-metals is lustrous (shiny)?
questions.explanation: Iodine is a non-metal with a shining surface. Most non-metals are dull.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The property of metals by which they can be beaten into thin sheets is called:
questions.explanation: Malleability is the property of being hammered into thin sheets. Aluminium and silver foil are examples.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Solid non-metals such as sulphur are generally:
questions.explanation: Solid non-metals break into pieces when hammered, so they are brittle.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following metals reacts the most vigorously with cold water?
questions.explanation: Sodium reacts violently with water. Copper and gold do not react with it.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is a displacement reaction? Give an example involving a metal.
questions.answer: A displacement reaction is one in which a more reactive metal pushes out a less reactive metal from its salt solution. For example, iron displaces copper from copper sulphate solution.
keyPoints: More reactive metal displaces less reactive metal
From a solution of its salt
Example with iron and copper sulphate
questions.explanation: Reactivity decides which metal is displaced.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A dull, grey piece of an old metal object becomes shiny after rubbing with sandpaper. The reason is that:
options: The metal changes into a non-metal
Heat is added to the metal
A dull layer of oxide or tarnish on the surface was rubbed off
questions.explanation: Metals form a dull coat on the surface by reacting with air, and rubbing removes it to show the shiny metal.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Aluminium foil is used for wrapping food because it:
options: Can be rolled into very thin sheets and does not readily react with food
questions.explanation: Aluminium is malleable and fairly unreactive, so it is suitable for wrapping food.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Name two ways to prevent iron objects from rusting and explain how one of them works.
questions.answer: Rusting can be prevented by painting or by oiling and greasing the iron. These coatings keep air and moisture away from the surface, and iron needs both to rust.
keyPoints: Coating keeps out air and moisture
Rusting needs both oxygen and water
questions.explanation: Rusting is prevented by stopping contact with air and water.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: LPG stands for:
questions.explanation: LPG, used for cooking, is a petroleum product stored as a liquid under pressure.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Coal is mostly made of:
questions.explanation: Coal contains a large amount of carbon.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The slow conversion of dead vegetation into coal over millions of years is called:
questions.explanation: Carbonisation is the slow change of buried plant matter into coal.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What are fossil fuels? Name two.
questions.answer: Fossil fuels are fuels formed from the remains of dead plants and animals buried under the earth for millions of years. Coal and petroleum are examples.
keyPoints: Formed from dead plants and animals
questions.explanation: Fossil fuels are limited resources.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In a petroleum refinery, the different products are separated from crude oil on the basis of their different:
questions.explanation: Heating crude oil makes its parts boil off at different temperatures, so each can be collected separately.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Coal and petroleum will not last forever because:
options: They are present only in the sea
The rate at which we use them is much greater than the rate at which they form
questions.explanation: They take millions of years to form but are being consumed quickly.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Mention three ways in which a driver can save petrol or diesel.
questions.answer: A driver can switch off the engine at traffic lights, drive at a steady moderate speed and keep the tyres inflated to the correct pressure. Regular servicing of the vehicle also saves fuel.
keyPoints: Switch off engine at red light
questions.explanation: Saving fuel reduces pollution and cost.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is a feature of an ideal fuel?
options: It is cheap, easily available and burns easily without harmful products
It produces a lot of smoke
It burns only at very high temperatures
questions.explanation: A good fuel should be cheap, easy to get and burn cleanly.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is a gaseous fuel?
questions.explanation: LPG is a fuel that is a gas at ordinary pressure.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In a candle flame, the bright yellow middle zone is due to:
options: Partial burning of the fuel, in which tiny unburnt carbon particles glow
questions.explanation: The middle zone has partial combustion and glowing carbon particles, so it is bright.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: State the three ways of putting out a fire.
questions.answer: A fire can be put out by cutting off the supply of air (oxygen), removing the fuel, or cooling the fuel below its ignition temperature. For example, water cools the burning material.
questions.explanation: Removing any one of the three requirements stops the fire.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Oil in a frying pan catches fire. What is the safest first action?
options: Cover the pan with a lid
questions.explanation: A lid cuts off the air, so the fire goes out. Water would spread burning oil.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A gas stove gives more heat than burning the same mass of wood. This is because LPG has:
options: A higher calorific value than wood
questions.explanation: A fuel with a higher calorific value gives more heat per kilogram.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: How does burning of fuels contribute to global warming?
questions.answer: Burning fuels such as coal, petrol and diesel releases carbon dioxide into the air. Carbon dioxide traps heat in the atmosphere, so increased amounts raise the temperature of the Earth.
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide is a greenhouse gas.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A large area set aside to conserve wild animals, plants and their habitat, where private activities such as grazing and cultivation are not allowed, is a:
questions.explanation: National parks are strictly protected areas for wildlife and natural vegetation.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Project Tiger was started to:
options: Protect tigers and their habitats in India
questions.explanation: Project Tiger is a conservation programme to protect tigers and the forests in which they live.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is a cause of extinction of animal species?
questions.explanation: Poaching kills animals for skin, horn or ivory and can wipe out a species.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Give two reasons why forests are important.
questions.answer: Forests are home to many plants and animals. They give us wood, medicines and food, prevent soil erosion, and absorb carbon dioxide while releasing oxygen.
questions.explanation: Forests support life and the environment.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why is destruction of habitat a major threat to wild animals?
options: They lose their food, shelter and breeding places
questions.explanation: Animals depend on their habitat for food, water, shelter and breeding.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: If all the snakes in a field are killed, what is most likely to happen?
options: The number of frogs will not change
The number of rats may increase and damage the crop
questions.explanation: Snakes feed on rats. Without them, rats can multiply and damage grain.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Suggest three ways in which students can help to protect forests and wildlife.
questions.answer: Students can plant and take care of trees, avoid wasting paper, and refuse to buy products made from wild animals. They can also spread awareness about not littering or disturbing forests.
keyPoints: Do not buy wildlife products or spread awareness
questions.explanation: Small actions by many people help conservation.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is found only in plant cells?
questions.explanation: A cell wall is found around plant cells and not animal cells.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Cells can be seen with the help of a:
questions.explanation: Most cells are too small to be seen with the naked eye and are studied with a microscope.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The genes that pass on features from parents to children are present on the:
questions.explanation: Chromosomes in the nucleus are made of genes.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Write the function of the nucleus and the cytoplasm.
questions.answer: The nucleus controls all the activities of the cell and holds the chromosomes. The cytoplasm is the jelly-like part in which the organelles lie and where many chemical reactions of the cell take place.
keyPoints: Nucleus controls the cell and holds chromosomes
questions.explanation: Both are essential parts of every cell.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A scientist finds that a cell has a cell wall, chloroplasts and a large vacuole. The cell most likely came from:
questions.explanation: Cell wall, chloroplasts and a large vacuole are typical features of plant cells.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which statement about the cell membrane is correct?
options: It is present only in plant cells
It is a thick rigid layer outside every cell
It is present in both plant and animal cells and controls what enters and leaves
questions.explanation: All cells have a cell membrane around the cytoplasm.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is the function of the large vacuole in a plant cell?
questions.answer: The vacuole stores water, food and waste substances. It also keeps the cell firm because it is filled with fluid pressing on the cell wall.
questions.explanation: A large central vacuole is typical of mature plant cells.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The change of a tadpole into an adult frog is called:
questions.explanation: Metamorphosis is the change in body form during development.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A zygote divides repeatedly and forms a ball of cells called the:
questions.explanation: The zygote divides to form an embryo.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following animals lays eggs (is oviparous)?
questions.explanation: A hen lays eggs, while dogs, cats and cows give birth to young ones.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is the difference between oviparous and viviparous animals? Give one example of each.
questions.answer: Oviparous animals lay eggs, and the young develop outside the mother's body, for example hens. Viviparous animals give birth to young ones that have developed inside the mother, for example cows or humans.
keyPoints: Viviparous give birth to young ones
questions.explanation: They differ in where the young develop.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Millions of sperms are released in humans, though only one sperm fertilises an egg. Why?
options: The egg needs many sperms to grow
Many sperms are lost or die on the way, so a large number increases the chance of fertilisation
The body cannot stop producing them
questions.explanation: Only a few of the many sperms reach the egg.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which statement about asexual reproduction is correct?
options: It needs both male and female gametes
The offspring look very different from the parent
questions.explanation: In asexual reproduction a single parent gives rise to offspring, as in Hydra and Amoeba.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Describe how a fertilised egg develops into a baby in humans.
questions.answer: The zygote divides repeatedly to form an embryo, which gets attached to the wall of the uterus. The embryo develops body parts, and after the stage called foetus the baby is born after about nine months.
keyPoints: Foetus develops and baby is born
questions.explanation: Development takes place in the uterus.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is a change in girls during puberty?
questions.explanation: The development of breasts is a change seen in girls at puberty.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The thyroid gland is located in the:
