questions.explanation: The thyroid gland lies in the neck.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Insulin is produced by the:
questions.explanation: The pancreas produces insulin, which controls the sugar level in blood.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is the difference between primary and secondary sexual characters?
questions.answer: Primary sexual characters are the sex organs present from birth, such as testes and ovaries. Secondary sexual characters appear at puberty, such as a beard in boys and development of breasts in girls.
keyPoints: Primary: sex organs present from birth
questions.explanation: Secondary characters develop under the influence of hormones.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why is the use of iodised salt recommended?
options: Iodine in it is needed by the thyroid to make thyroxine and prevents goitre
questions.explanation: Thyroxine needs iodine, so a shortage of iodine causes goitre.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Rahul feels moody and irritable during adolescence. What is the most likely explanation?
options: Hormonal changes in the body at this age can affect mood
He is ill with a serious infection
He has a vitamin deficiency only
He has a defect in his eyes
questions.explanation: Mood swings are common during adolescence due to hormonal changes.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why is personal hygiene especially important during adolescence?
questions.answer: At puberty the sweat glands become more active and the skin becomes oily, which can cause body odour and pimples. Bathing daily, wearing clean clothes and keeping the skin clean prevent infections.
questions.explanation: Good hygiene keeps adolescents healthy.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is a type of friction?
questions.explanation: Static, sliding and rolling are the types of friction.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The unit of pressure is the:
questions.explanation: Pressure is measured in pascals (Pa), where 1 Pa is 1 N per square metre.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The pressure of the atmosphere acts:
questions.explanation: Air presses on objects from all sides.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why do deep-sea divers wear special suits?
questions.answer: Pressure in water increases with depth, so at great depth the pressure on the body is very large. A special suit protects the diver from this high pressure.
keyPoints: Very high pressure at great depth
questions.explanation: Liquid pressure rises with depth.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: When you drink through a straw, the liquid rises because:
options: The liquid is lighter than air
Pressure inside the mouth is reduced, and atmospheric pressure pushes the liquid up
questions.explanation: Sucking lowers pressure in the straw, and the higher atmospheric pressure on the liquid pushes it up.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: It is easier to move a heavy load on a cart with wheels than to drag it on the ground because:
options: Rolling friction is much less than sliding friction
questions.explanation: Rolling friction is smaller than sliding friction.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why do we sprinkle fine powder on a carrom board before playing?
questions.answer: The powder forms a thin layer between the board and the striker or coins, which reduces friction. The pieces then slide easily and smoothly over the board.
questions.explanation: Powders and oils act as lubricants.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In the human ear, which part starts vibrating when sound waves strike it?
questions.explanation: The eardrum is a thin stretched membrane that vibrates when sound waves reach it.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Sound cannot travel through:
questions.explanation: Sound needs a medium, and a vacuum is empty.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Sounds of frequency higher than 20,000 Hz are called:
questions.explanation: Ultrasonic sounds are above the audible range of humans.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Distinguish between music and noise.
questions.answer: Music is a pleasant sound produced by vibrations that are regular and well arranged. Noise is an unpleasant sound with irregular vibrations.
questions.explanation: What is pleasant depends on the type of vibration.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A ruler is held on a table with part of it hanging over the edge and plucked. If more of the ruler is slid out over the edge, the sound will have:
questions.explanation: A longer vibrating part vibrates more slowly, so the frequency and pitch are lower.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A person who puts an ear on a railway track can hear an approaching train before it can be heard through air. This is because:
options: Sound travels faster in solids than in air
The train makes more sound on the track
questions.explanation: Sound travels faster in a solid such as steel than in air.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Describe the path of sound through the human ear in simple steps.
questions.answer: Sound waves enter the ear canal from the pinna and make the eardrum vibrate. The vibrations are passed on through the middle ear to the inner ear, and nerves carry the message to the brain.
keyPoints: Sound enters through pinna and ear canal
Nerves carry signals to the brain
questions.explanation: The ear converts vibrations to nerve signals.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following does NOT conduct electricity?
questions.explanation: Distilled water has no dissolved salts, so it does not conduct. Tap water contains salts and does.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Materials through which electric current can pass are called:
questions.explanation: Conductors allow current to flow through them.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In copper plating, a solution of copper sulphate is used because it:
options: Provides copper that is deposited on the object
questions.explanation: Copper from the solution is deposited on the article to be plated.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: When current is passed through acidified water, more bubbles are seen at the negative electrode. The gas there is:
questions.explanation: Water splits into hydrogen and oxygen, and hydrogen is released at the negative electrode.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Give two uses of electroplating.
questions.answer: Electroplating is used to give a shiny, attractive finish to objects such as jewellery and car parts. It is also used to protect metals like iron from rusting, for example by chromium or tin plating.
questions.explanation: A thin coat of metal changes the surface of an object.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A tester bulb does not glow when its ends are dipped in a liquid. Which conclusion is the most reasonable?
options: The liquid is a very strong conductor
The liquid may be a poor conductor, and a more sensitive LED tester can be tried
questions.explanation: A weak current may be too small to light a bulb but can light an LED.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Testing a liquid using a cell is safe, but testing it with the household mains supply is dangerous because:
options: A cell has a low voltage, whereas the mains has a high voltage that can give a serious shock
questions.explanation: The voltage of a cell is low and safe, but mains voltage can be fatal.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why does salt solution conduct electricity while pure distilled water and sugar solution do not?
questions.answer: Salt dissolves in water to give charged particles that can carry the current through the liquid. Distilled water and sugar solution have no such charged particles, so they do not conduct.
keyPoints: Distilled water and sugar solution lack them
questions.explanation: A liquid conducts only if it has charged particles that are free to move.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: An object becomes electrically charged when:
options: It is rubbed with another suitable object
questions.explanation: Rubbing two different objects together can transfer charge and charge them.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The Earth's crust is made of broken parts called:
questions.explanation: The Earth's outermost layer is divided into moving plates, and their movements cause earthquakes.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A girl stands 2 m in front of a plane mirror. Her image appears at a distance of how much behind the mirror?
questions.explanation: The image in a plane mirror is as far behind the mirror as the object is in front.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A kaleidoscope produces beautiful patterns because of:
questions.explanation: Mirrors inclined at an angle give many images by repeated reflection.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: How does a periscope help us to see over an obstacle?
questions.answer: A periscope has two plane mirrors fixed at 45 degrees at its two ends. Light from the object reflects from the top mirror to the lower mirror and then to the eye, so we can see objects over a wall.
keyPoints: Two plane mirrors at the ends
questions.explanation: Periscopes use the reflection of light.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: When white light passes through a prism, which colour bends the most?
questions.explanation: Violet bends the most and red the least, so the colours spread out.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A disc painted with the seven rainbow colours is spun very fast. It appears:
questions.explanation: The colours blend in the eye and the disc appears nearly white (Newton's disc).

questions.subject: science
questions.q: We can see our image in a plane mirror but cannot catch it on a screen. Why?
questions.answer: The image in a plane mirror is virtual. It is formed behind the mirror where light rays only appear to meet, so it cannot be obtained on a screen.
questions.explanation: Real images can be caught on a screen, but virtual ones cannot.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which is the first step in the production of a crop?
questions.explanation: The soil must be prepared by ploughing and levelling before seeds are sown.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is used traditionally to turn and loosen the soil in a field?
questions.explanation: A plough, pulled by animals or a tractor, is used for tilling the soil.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Urea, a common chemical fertiliser, mainly supplies the crop with:
questions.explanation: Urea is rich in nitrogen, which plants need to make proteins and to grow leaves.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Write two differences between manure and a chemical fertiliser.
questions.answer: Manure is made from the decomposition of plant and animal waste, while a fertiliser is a man-made chemical produced in factories. Manure adds humus to the soil but a fertiliser does not, and a fertiliser is richer in particular nutrients.
keyPoints: Manure is natural; fertiliser is man-made
Fertiliser is rich in specific nutrients
questions.explanation: Both supply nutrients, but in different ways.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which practice helps to restore nitrogen in the soil without using a fertiliser?
options: Growing the same cereal every year
Growing a pulse crop in rotation with cereals
questions.explanation: Pulse plants have bacteria in their roots that fix nitrogen, so they enrich the soil.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: If seeds are sown very close to each other, the result is likely to be:
options: Competition for water, nutrients and light, leading to weak plants
questions.explanation: Crowded seedlings compete for resources, so each plant grows poorly.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why are rabi crops such as wheat sown in winter and kharif crops such as paddy in the rainy season?
questions.answer: Rabi crops need a cool growing period and little water, so they grow well in winter. Kharif crops need warm weather and plenty of water, which the monsoon rains supply.
keyPoints: Kharif crops need warmth and abundant water
Rains supply water to kharif crops
questions.explanation: Each crop is suited to the weather of its season.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Microorganisms are so small that they can be seen only with the help of a:
questions.explanation: Microorganisms are too tiny for the naked eye.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is an alga?
questions.explanation: Spirogyra is a green alga found in ponds.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The antibiotic penicillin is obtained from a:
questions.explanation: Penicillin is made by Penicillium, a fungus.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Write two harmful effects of microorganisms.
questions.answer: Some microorganisms cause diseases in humans, animals and plants, such as cholera and typhoid. Others spoil food, making it unsafe to eat and causing food poisoning.
questions.explanation: Harmful microbes are called pathogens when they cause disease.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why can eating spoilt food lead to food poisoning?
options: Spoilt food has too many vitamins
Microorganisms growing on it release toxic substances
The food has become too soft
It has lost all its water
questions.explanation: Microbes growing on food produce toxins that can make us ill.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why is sugar used to preserve jams and squashes?
options: It reduces the moisture, so microorganisms cannot grow
questions.explanation: A high sugar content draws out water, which stops the growth of microbes.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: How can the spread of cholera be prevented in a village?
questions.answer: The water should be boiled or purified before drinking, and food must be covered and kept clean. People should wash hands before eating, and waste should be disposed of properly so that flies do not carry germs.
questions.explanation: Cholera spreads through contaminated water and food.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: PVC is commonly used to make:
questions.explanation: PVC is a strong plastic used for pipes and for covering electric wires.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following fibres is made from petroleum products?
questions.explanation: Polyester is a synthetic fibre made from petrochemicals. Cotton, wool and silk are natural.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Fishing nets and tyre cords are made of nylon mainly because it has:
questions.explanation: Nylon is very strong, elastic and does not wear out easily.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Write two uses of nylon.
questions.answer: Nylon is used to make ropes, fishing nets and parachutes because it is strong and light. It is also used to make toothbrush bristles, socks and tents.
keyPoints: Other items such as toothbrush bristles
questions.explanation: Nylon's strength decides its uses.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Plastic cooking utensils are not placed on a flame because:
options: They can melt or burn, and spoil the food
questions.explanation: Plastics soften or burn at high temperatures.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why is burning plastic waste harmful?
options: It releases poisonous gases into the air
questions.explanation: Burning plastics releases poisonous fumes that pollute the air.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Plastics are both useful and harmful. Explain with two points each.
questions.answer: Plastics are useful because they are light, cheap and strong, and they do not rust. They are harmful because they are non-biodegradable and pollute the land and water, and burning them gives poisonous gases.
questions.explanation: Their proper use and disposal is important.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which non-metal present in air is needed by living things for breathing?
questions.explanation: Oxygen in the air is needed for respiration.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Metals are generally:
options: Poor conductors of heat and electricity
Good conductors of heat and electricity
questions.explanation: Most metals conduct heat and electricity well and are shiny and malleable.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Oxides of metals are generally:
questions.explanation: Metal oxides are basic in nature, whereas non-metal oxides are acidic.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why are iron and steel used in building bridges and buildings?
questions.answer: Iron and steel are very strong and hard and have high melting points. They can be shaped into beams and rods, so they can carry large loads.
questions.explanation: The properties of metals decide their use.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A piece of iron and a piece of sulphur are dropped into separate test tubes of dilute hydrochloric acid. What is observed?
options: Iron reacts and gives off hydrogen, but sulphur does not react
questions.explanation: Metals such as iron react with dilute acid to release hydrogen. Non-metals such as sulphur do not.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Mercury is used in some thermometers because it:
options: Is a gas at room temperature
Is a liquid metal at room temperature and expands evenly on heating
questions.explanation: Mercury remains liquid at ordinary temperatures and expands steadily with heat.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A metal spoon left in a cup of hot tea soon becomes hot. Explain why.
questions.answer: Metals are good conductors of heat. The heat of the tea passes through the metal spoon by conduction from the hot end to the end held in the hand.
keyPoints: Metals are good conductors of heat
questions.explanation: A plastic spoon would stay cooler.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The hard, porous, black solid obtained by heating coal strongly in the absence of air is called:
questions.explanation: Coke is a tough, porous residue made by heating coal in the absence of air.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The thick, black liquid obtained during the processing of coal is called:
questions.explanation: Coal tar is a black, thick liquid with a strong smell, used to make paints, dyes and other products.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which gas obtained during processing of coal is used as a fuel in industries near coal processing plants?
questions.explanation: Coal gas is produced when coal is processed and is used as a fuel in industries.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which petroleum product is used as a fuel for heavy vehicles such as trucks and buses?
questions.explanation: Diesel is used in trucks, buses and trains.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is natural gas? Mention two of its uses.
questions.answer: Natural gas is a fossil fuel found trapped with petroleum, and its main constituent is methane. It is used as a fuel (as CNG in vehicles) and as a starting material for making fertilisers and other chemicals.
keyPoints: Uses such as CNG and chemicals
questions.explanation: Natural gas is a cleaner fossil fuel.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: LPG is preferred to wood as a domestic fuel mainly because it:
options: Burns with little smoke and has a high calorific value
questions.explanation: LPG burns cleanly with little smoke and gives a large amount of heat.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A person smells gas in the kitchen and suspects an LPG leak. What should be done first?
options: Switch on the exhaust fan with the electrical switch
Open the windows and doors and avoid using any electrical switch or flame
questions.explanation: Ventilating the room without any spark prevents the gas from catching fire.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is the difference between renewable and non-renewable resources? Give an example of each.
questions.answer: Renewable resources can be replaced by nature in a short time, such as sunlight and wind. Non-renewable resources take millions of years to form and will get exhausted, such as coal and petroleum.
keyPoints: Non-renewable: limited and take millions of years
questions.explanation: Fossil fuels are non-renewable.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: When a fuel containing carbon burns completely, the main products are:
questions.explanation: Complete combustion of a carbon fuel gives carbon dioxide and water, with heat and light.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which gas supports combustion?
questions.explanation: Oxygen is the supporter of combustion.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is a solid fuel?
questions.explanation: Coke is a solid fuel. LPG is a gas, and kerosene and petrol are liquids.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of these has the highest calorific value?
questions.explanation: LPG releases more heat per kilogram than coal, wood or dung cakes.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is an explosion? Why are firecrackers dangerous?
questions.answer: An explosion is a sudden reaction in which a large amount of heat, light, sound and gas is produced. Firecrackers can burn the skin, hurt the eyes and ears, cause fires and pollute the air, so they must be used with care.
keyPoints: Sudden reaction with heat, light, sound and gas
questions.explanation: Explosive substances release energy very quickly.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following actions would reduce air pollution caused by burning fuels?
options: Burning more wood in open fires
questions.explanation: CNG burns more cleanly than petrol or diesel.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A piece of wood burns slowly, but fine wood shavings burn quickly. The reason is that shavings:
options: Have a larger surface exposed to the air
questions.explanation: More surface exposed to oxygen allows faster burning.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: How does a carbon dioxide fire extinguisher put out a fire?
questions.answer: Carbon dioxide is heavier than air, so it covers the burning material like a blanket and cuts off the supply of oxygen. It also cools the fuel as it comes out of the cylinder.
keyPoints: Carbon dioxide is heavier than air
Covers the fire like a blanket
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide is also useful as it does not harm electrical equipment.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The variety of plants and animals found in an area is called:
questions.explanation: Biodiversity is the variety of living things in a region.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The place where a plant or animal lives naturally is called its:
questions.explanation: A habitat is the natural home of an organism.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Large-scale deforestation in a region can reduce its:
questions.explanation: Fewer trees mean less transpiration and fewer rain clouds, so rainfall may fall.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The main reasons why many animals migrate are:
options: Better climate, food or a place to breed
questions.explanation: Migration takes animals to places suitable for food, weather or breeding.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Write the difference between a wildlife sanctuary and a national park.
questions.answer: In a wildlife sanctuary, animals are protected from hunting, but some human activities may be allowed. A national park is a more strictly protected area in which activities like grazing and cultivation are not allowed.
keyPoints: Some human activity may be allowed in sanctuaries
National park is more strictly protected
questions.explanation: Both help to conserve wildlife.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A paper factory needs a lot of wood. Which approach helps to keep forests safe?
options: Cut trees and also plant new saplings (reforestation)
Stop all use of paper only
questions.explanation: Replanting trees keeps the forest cover from shrinking.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why is it important to conserve biodiversity?
options: All species in an ecosystem depend on one another, so loss of one affects others
Plants are not part of biodiversity
Species do not depend on each other
questions.explanation: Living things are linked in food chains and webs.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Explain how deforestation can lead to a shortage of water or drought in an area.
questions.answer: Trees take water from the soil and release it into the air, which helps to form rain. Without trees there is less rainfall, and the water runs off the bare soil quickly instead of soaking in, so the area becomes dry.
questions.explanation: Forests play a major role in the water cycle.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The cell wall of plant cells is made of:
questions.explanation: Cellulose makes the cell wall rigid.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The green pigment that traps sunlight is present in:
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll in chloroplasts traps sunlight for photosynthesis.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is a multicellular organism?
questions.explanation: A banyan tree has billions of cells. The others consist of a single cell.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following shows the correct order of organisation in a multicellular organism, from simplest to most complex?
questions.explanation: Cells form tissues, tissues form organs, and organs work together as organ systems.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Name any three parts of an animal cell and write one function of each.
questions.answer: The cell membrane controls entry and exit of substances. The nucleus controls the activities of the cell. The cytoplasm holds the organelles and is the place of many reactions.
questions.explanation: Any three correct parts are accepted.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A slide of human cheek cells is seen under a microscope. Which of the following would you find?
options: A nucleus and cell membrane but no cell wall
questions.explanation: Animal cells have a nucleus and a membrane, but no cell wall or chloroplasts.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A plant wilts if it is not watered. The main reason is that its cells:
options: Lose water from the vacuoles and lose their firmness
questions.explanation: When the vacuoles lose water, the cells become soft and the plant droops.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: An Amoeba is a single cell, yet it is a complete living organism. Explain.
questions.answer: A single cell of Amoeba carries out all the life processes itself, such as taking in food, respiration, getting rid of waste, movement and reproduction. It does not need other cells for these functions.
keyPoints: One cell performs all life processes
questions.explanation: Unicellular organisms are complete living beings.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The male reproductive organ that produces sperms is the:
questions.explanation: Testes (singular testis) produce sperms.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Reproductive cells (sperms and eggs) are together called:
questions.explanation: Gametes are the sex cells used in sexual reproduction.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following animals shows metamorphosis?
questions.explanation: A butterfly changes from egg to larva to pupa to adult.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following shows internal fertilisation?
questions.explanation: Cows fertilise eggs inside the female body. Frogs, toads and most bony fish fertilise outside the body.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Name the male reproductive organs and state the functions of the testes.
questions.answer: The male reproductive system has a pair of testes, sperm ducts and a penis. The testes produce sperms and the male hormone testosterone.
questions.explanation: The testes are the main organs of the male reproductive system.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A hen sits on its eggs for about three weeks. The main purpose is to:
options: Keep the eggs warm so that the embryos can develop into chicks
questions.explanation: Warmth is necessary for the embryo inside a fertilised egg to grow.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Identical twins are formed when:
options: Two different eggs are fertilised by two sperms
A single fertilised egg splits into two embryos
questions.explanation: A zygote that divides into two separate embryos gives identical twins.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why is internal fertilisation more dependable than external fertilisation?
questions.answer: In internal fertilisation the sperms are released inside the female body, so they are close to the egg and well protected, giving a good chance of fertilisation. Fewer eggs are needed, and the young are often cared for.
keyPoints: Sperms close to egg inside the body
questions.explanation: External fertilisation is more chancy.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The sudden rapid increase in height during adolescence is called:
questions.explanation: A growth spurt is the quick growth in height at the start of adolescence.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The voice box is also known as the:
questions.explanation: The larynx holds the vocal cords.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which hormone from the pituitary gland controls the growth of the body?
questions.explanation: The pituitary releases growth hormone that controls growth of the body.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Menstruation occurs when:
options: The egg released from the ovary is not fertilised and the lining of the uterus breaks down
questions.explanation: If the egg is not fertilised, the thick lining of the uterus is shed with blood.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is menstruation? At what stage of life does it begin and stop?
questions.answer: Menstruation is the monthly flow of blood and tissue from the uterus when an egg is not fertilised. It begins at puberty and stops around the age of 45 to 50 years.
questions.explanation: The cycle is controlled by hormones.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The menstrual cycle does not occur in a woman during pregnancy because:
options: The egg that was released was fertilised and the uterus lining is kept for the baby
questions.explanation: After fertilisation, the thick lining of the uterus nourishes the developing embryo.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why is it advised to eat iron-rich food such as green leafy vegetables during adolescence?
options: Iron helps make haemoglobin in the blood and prevents anaemia
questions.explanation: Iron is needed for haemoglobin in red blood cells.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Explain why the pituitary gland is important at puberty.
questions.answer: The pituitary gland releases hormones that make the testes and ovaries start producing sex hormones, and it also releases the hormone for growth. In this way it controls the changes at puberty.
questions.explanation: It is called the master gland.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The force that pulls objects towards the Earth is called:
questions.explanation: Gravity is the force of attraction of the Earth.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Friction is a force that acts between:
questions.explanation: Friction opposes the relative motion of two surfaces that touch each other.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The pressure on a surface increases when:
options: The same force acts on a smaller area
The same force acts on a bigger area
The force is reduced and the area is the same
questions.explanation: Pressure equals force divided by area, so a smaller area gives higher pressure.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is atmospheric pressure? Why do we not feel it?
questions.answer: Atmospheric pressure is the pressure exerted by the air around us. We do not feel it because the pressure of the fluids inside our bodies balances it.
questions.explanation: Air has weight and exerts pressure.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A person exerts more pressure on the ground when standing on one foot than on both feet because:
options: The area of contact is halved, so the pressure doubles
questions.explanation: The same weight acts on half the area, so the pressure is twice as much.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Tractors have very wide tyres because:
options: They spread the weight over a larger area and reduce the pressure on the soil
questions.explanation: Wide tyres decrease pressure on the ground, so the tractor does not sink in soft soil.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why do nails and drawing pins have pointed tips?
questions.answer: A pointed tip has a very small area, so when force is applied the pressure is large, and the nail easily goes into the wood or board.
questions.explanation: Pressure is inversely related to area.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The time taken for one complete vibration is called the:
questions.explanation: Time period is the time for one oscillation.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following produces sound by a vibrating string?
questions.explanation: A sitar has strings that vibrate. A drum uses a stretched membrane, and a flute an air column.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following sounds is likely to have the highest pitch?
options: The beat of a bass drum
questions.explanation: A mosquito's wings vibrate very fast, so its sound has a high frequency.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is amplitude? How does it affect the sound we hear?
questions.answer: Amplitude is the maximum displacement of a vibrating object from its rest position. A larger amplitude produces a louder sound and a smaller amplitude a softer sound.
questions.explanation: Loudness depends on the amplitude.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: An object vibrates 200 times in half a second. What is its frequency?
questions.explanation: Frequency is the number of vibrations per second, which is 200 divided by 0.5 = 400 Hz.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following frequencies cannot be heard by a normal human ear?
questions.explanation: The audible range is about 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz, so 25,000 Hz is above it.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In a guitar, how can the pitch of the sound from a string be made higher?
questions.answer: The pitch becomes higher when the string is tightened, shortened or replaced by a thinner string, because it then vibrates with a higher frequency.
keyPoints: Shorten the string or use a thinner one
questions.explanation: Pitch depends on frequency.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Electric current flows in a circuit only when the circuit is:
questions.explanation: The path must be continuous for current to flow.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is a good conductor of electricity?
questions.explanation: Copper is a metal and allows current to pass easily.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: During copper plating, copper is deposited on the:
questions.explanation: The metal is deposited on the electrode connected to the negative terminal of the battery.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is the difference between a conductor and an insulator? Give an example of each.
questions.answer: A conductor allows electric current to pass through it, for example copper. An insulator does not allow current to pass through, for example rubber.
questions.explanation: Most metals are conductors.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: When a liquid is placed in a tester circuit, the bulb glows only dimly. This suggests that the liquid is:
questions.explanation: A dim glow means only a small current is passing.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why is it unsafe to use electrical appliances with wet hands or near water?
options: Water that contains dissolved salts conducts electricity and can cause a shock
questions.explanation: Ordinary water conducts current, so there is a risk of a shock.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Describe briefly how a spoon can be electroplated with silver.
questions.answer: The spoon is made the negative electrode (cathode) and a silver plate is the positive electrode (anode) in a solution of a silver salt. When electric current is passed, silver from the solution is deposited on the spoon.
keyPoints: Silver plate is the anode in a silver salt solution
Current deposits silver on the spoon
questions.explanation: The set-up is a type of electrolysis.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In the colours of a rainbow, orange comes immediately after:
questions.explanation: The order is violet, indigo, blue, green, yellow, orange and red.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The point on the Earth's surface directly above the place where an earthquake starts is called the:
questions.explanation: The epicentre lies directly above the focus where the earthquake begins.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: If a ray of light strikes a plane mirror at an angle of incidence of 30 degrees, the angle of reflection will be:
questions.explanation: The angle of reflection equals the angle of incidence.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Write two precautions to be taken during a thunderstorm.
questions.answer: We should stay inside a building or a car and avoid standing under tall trees or in open fields. We should also avoid using electrical appliances and corded phones, and stay away from water.
keyPoints: Stay inside a building or vehicle
Avoid tall trees and open ground
questions.explanation: Lightning is attracted to tall objects.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which house design would be the safest in an earthquake-prone area?
options: A light building with a strong, flexible frame
A very heavy stone building with no frame
A tall building with heavy objects on the top
questions.explanation: Light, well-framed buildings are less likely to collapse during shaking.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A girl stands 3 m in front of a plane mirror and then walks 1 m toward it. What is the new distance between her and her image?
questions.explanation: She is now 2 m from the mirror and the image is 2 m behind it, so they are 4 m apart.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A balloon is rubbed against hair and then sticks to a wall. Explain why.
questions.answer: Rubbing charges the balloon with static electricity. When the charged balloon is brought near the wall, it attracts opposite charge on the wall surface, so the balloon is held to it for some time.
keyPoints: Charged object induces opposite charge on the wall
questions.explanation: This is an example of static electricity.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is an oilseed crop?
questions.explanation: Groundnut seeds are crushed to obtain oil, so it is an oilseed crop.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A sickle is a farm tool used for:
questions.explanation: A sickle has a curved blade and is used to cut mature crops by hand.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The sprinkler system of irrigation is most useful for:
options: Uneven land where water is scarce
questions.explanation: A sprinkler gives water like rain, so it suits uneven land and saves water.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Fertilisers are added to the soil mainly to:
options: Replace the nutrients that earlier crops have taken
Increase the number of earthworms only
questions.explanation: Crops take nutrients from the soil, and fertilisers and manure put them back.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is threshing, and how is it done on large farms?
questions.answer: Threshing is the separation of grain seeds from the dry stalks and husk of the harvested crop. On large farms it is done with a machine called a combine harvester, which also harvests the crop.
keyPoints: Separating grain from stalks and husk
questions.explanation: On small farms it can be done by beating the crop by hand.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A field has become less fertile after chemical fertilisers have been used alone for many years. What is the best remedy?
options: Add more of the same fertiliser
Add manure and rotate the crops
questions.explanation: Manure adds humus, and crop rotation restores nutrients.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Weeds should be removed from a crop field early because weeds:
options: Compete with the crop for nutrients, water and light, and may harbour pests
questions.explanation: Weeds take away resources and reduce the yield of the crop.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why do seeds need water in order to germinate?
questions.answer: Seeds take in water, which softens the seed coat and wakes up the embryo inside. The water also helps the stored food to be used by the growing seedling.
keyPoints: Stored food is used by the seedling
questions.explanation: Without water a seed remains dormant.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is a protozoan?
questions.explanation: Amoeba is a single-celled protozoan.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Medicines that kill or stop the growth of bacteria are called:
questions.explanation: Antibiotics act against bacteria.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Yeast is used in the commercial production of:
questions.explanation: Yeast ferments sugar into alcohol, which is used to make wine and beer.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Dengue is spread by the:
questions.explanation: The Aedes mosquito carries the dengue virus.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Name three methods of preserving food at home and say how each works.
questions.answer: Heating or cooking and refrigeration keep microbes from growing. Salting and adding sugar remove water, and adding oil or vinegar in pickles keeps air and microbes away.
questions.explanation: Preservation prevents spoilage by microorganisms.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Sodium benzoate is added to jams and squashes in small amounts to:
questions.explanation: Chemical preservatives slow or stop the growth of microbes in food.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why are children given vaccines at an early age?
options: To prepare their body to fight diseases before they get infected
To cure a disease they already have
questions.explanation: Vaccines let the body make antibodies in advance.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why is it important to wash hands with soap before eating?
questions.answer: Our hands pick up microbes from the surroundings. Washing with soap removes them, so they do not enter the body with the food and cause diseases such as diarrhoea.
questions.explanation: Hygiene prevents the spread of germs.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Fibres that are made from chemical substances in factories are called:
questions.explanation: Synthetic fibres are man-made, from chemicals.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which plastic is used to coat non-stick cookware?
questions.explanation: Teflon is slippery and heat resistant, so it is used as a non-stick coating.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which statement about polyester fabric is correct?
options: It absorbs a lot of water
It is made from a plant
It is heavy and always crumples
It is wrinkle-resistant and easy to wash
questions.explanation: Polyester crumples very little and dries fast, so it is popular for clothes.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is PET and what is it used for?
questions.answer: PET (polyethylene terephthalate) is a plastic that is light, strong and clear. It is used to make bottles and containers for drinks and food.
questions.explanation: PET is a widely used thermoplastic.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Shirts are often made from a blend of cotton and polyester because the blend:
options: Combines the comfort of cotton with the wrinkle resistance of polyester
questions.explanation: Blended fabrics combine useful properties of both fibres.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following habits helps to reduce plastic pollution?
options: Using a new plastic bag every time
questions.explanation: Reusing bags reduces the amount of plastic that is thrown away.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: How are synthetic fibres different from natural fibres in their source and properties?
questions.answer: Natural fibres such as cotton and wool come from plants and animals, whereas synthetic fibres such as nylon are made from chemicals in factories. Synthetic fibres are usually stronger, dry quickly and last longer, but they melt and catch fire easily.
keyPoints: Synthetic are strong, durable and quick drying but melt easily
questions.explanation: Both kinds have advantages and disadvantages.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following metals is commonly used to make jewellery?
questions.explanation: Gold is a shiny, soft and unreactive metal used in jewellery.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is a metal?
questions.explanation: Aluminium is a metal. Oxygen, carbon and sulphur are non-metals.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: When carbon burns in air, the gas produced is:
questions.explanation: Carbon combines with oxygen to form carbon dioxide.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Write two differences between metals and non-metals.
questions.answer: Metals are generally lustrous, malleable, ductile and good conductors of heat and electricity. Non-metals are generally dull, brittle if solid, and poor conductors of heat and electricity.
keyPoints: Metals are lustrous, malleable and ductile
Non-metals are dull, brittle and poor conductors
questions.explanation: There are a few exceptions, such as graphite and mercury.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A student tries to bend a copper wire and a piece of coal. The wire bends but the coal breaks. This shows that:
options: Metals are ductile and malleable, whereas coal is brittle
questions.explanation: Metals can be bent or drawn without breaking, but solid non-metals break easily.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A silver spoon left in the air for a long time becomes dark because:
options: It reacts with substances such as sulphur compounds in the air
The spoon gets heated by sunlight
questions.explanation: Silver forms a dark layer of tarnish by reacting with compounds in the air.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why are the handles of cooking pans made of plastic or wood instead of metal?
questions.answer: Metals are good conductors of heat, so a metal handle would become too hot to hold. Plastic and wood are poor conductors, so the handle remains cool enough to hold.
keyPoints: Plastic and wood are poor conductors
questions.explanation: Insulators keep the handle safe to touch.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Petrol, diesel and kerosene are obtained from:
questions.explanation: Crude petroleum is refined to get petrol, diesel and kerosene.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Coal is a:
questions.explanation: Coal is a black, hard, solid fuel.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which coal product is used for making naphthalene balls, dyes and paints?
questions.explanation: Many useful chemicals are made from coal tar.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: State two uses of coal.
questions.answer: Coal is used as a fuel in homes, in industries and in power plants to generate electricity. Its product, coke, is used in making steel.
questions.explanation: Coal is an important source of energy.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Compared with petrol, vehicles that run on CNG:
questions.explanation: CNG burns more completely and is a cleaner fuel.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In an oil-bearing rock, natural gas is found above the petroleum. This is because natural gas is:
questions.explanation: Natural gas is lighter than oil, so it collects above it.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why are coal and petroleum called fossil fuels?
questions.answer: They were formed from the remains of dead plants and animals, which were buried under the earth for millions of years. Heat and pressure turned them into fuels, as fossils form from old remains.
keyPoints: Formed from remains of dead organisms
questions.explanation: Fossil fuels are non-renewable.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The lowest temperature at which a substance catches fire is called its:
questions.explanation: Each substance has its own ignition temperature.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following catches fire very easily?
questions.explanation: Petrol has a very low ignition temperature and burns easily, so it is inflammable.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Water is a suitable extinguisher for burning wood and paper because it:
options: Cools the material below its ignition temperature
questions.explanation: Water absorbs heat and brings the temperature below ignition temperature.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Distinguish between combustible and non-combustible substances with two examples of each.
questions.answer: Combustible substances burn in air, such as wood and paper. Non-combustible substances do not burn, such as glass and stone.
questions.explanation: Combustibility depends on the substance.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Carbon monoxide, produced in incomplete combustion, is dangerous because it:
options: Is a poisonous gas that has no colour or smell
questions.explanation: Carbon monoxide cannot be seen or smelt, and it is poisonous when breathed.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why can sand be used to put out a small fire?
options: It cuts off the supply of air and covers the burning material
questions.explanation: Sand covers the fire and keeps oxygen from reaching it.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is calorific value? Why is it important when we choose a fuel?
questions.answer: Calorific value is the amount of heat produced by the complete burning of 1 kg of a fuel, measured in kJ/kg. A fuel with a higher calorific value gives more heat for the same mass, so it is more efficient.
keyPoints: Heat from complete burning of 1 kg
Higher value means a better fuel
questions.explanation: Fuels are compared by calorific value.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The plants and animals of a region are together called its:
questions.explanation: Flora refers to plants and fauna refers to animals.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Cutting down trees to get land for farming or buildings is called:
questions.explanation: Deforestation is the clearing of forests.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Animals that move from one region to another according to the season are called:
questions.explanation: Migratory animals travel regularly for food, climate or breeding.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is the Red Data Book and why is it important?
questions.answer: The Red Data Book is a record of species of plants and animals that are endangered or threatened with extinction. It helps in planning how to protect them.
questions.explanation: It is kept by conservation organisations.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which activity damages life in rivers and ponds the most?
options: Dumping industrial waste into the water
questions.explanation: Waste poisons the water and kills fish and plants.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why should we avoid buying articles made from animal skin or ivory?
options: Demand for them leads to poaching, which endangers species
questions.explanation: Buying them encourages hunting of wild animals.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: How can saving paper help to save forests?
questions.answer: Paper is made from wood pulp, which comes from trees. If we use less paper and reuse or recycle it, fewer trees are cut, so forests are protected.
keyPoints: Saving paper means fewer trees cut
questions.explanation: Reducing demand reduces cutting of forests.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The part of a plant cell that lies outside the cell membrane is the:
questions.explanation: The rigid cell wall surrounds the cell membrane in plant cells.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The genetic information of the cell is stored in the:
questions.explanation: The nucleus contains chromosomes carrying genes.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Compared with an animal cell, a mature plant cell typically has:
questions.explanation: Plant cells have a large central vacuole, while animal cells have small ones.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What are cell organelles? Name two of them.
questions.answer: Organelles are small structures within a cell, each doing a particular job. Two examples are the nucleus and the mitochondria.
questions.explanation: Organelles divide the work of the cell.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: An animal cell cannot make its own food by photosynthesis because it:
questions.explanation: Only cells with chloroplasts can trap sunlight to make food.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Cells in the roots of a plant have no chloroplasts. The most likely reason is that:
options: Sunlight does not reach the roots, so they do not carry out photosynthesis
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts are found where light reaches, as in leaves.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why is the nucleus called the control centre of a cell?
questions.answer: The nucleus holds the chromosomes with genes, which carry instructions for the cell, so it controls growth, activities and reproduction of the cell. A cell without its nucleus cannot work properly for long.
keyPoints: Controls the activities of the cell
Needed for the cell to function
questions.explanation: It acts like the brain of the cell.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The type of reproduction in which two parents are involved is called:
questions.explanation: Sexual reproduction needs a male and a female gamete.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The cell formed by fusion of a sperm and an egg is the:
questions.explanation: The fertilised egg is called a zygote.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The stage of development in humans in which all the body parts can be identified is the:
questions.explanation: The embryo is called a foetus once its body parts can be identified.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Write two differences between sexual and asexual reproduction.
questions.answer: In sexual reproduction two parents are involved and gametes fuse, so the young are different from the parents. In asexual reproduction only one parent is involved and the young are almost identical to the parent, as in Hydra budding.
keyPoints: Sexual needs two parents; asexual needs one
Asexual offspring are similar to the parent
questions.explanation: Asexual reproduction does not involve gametes.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Frogs usually lay their eggs in water in the rainy season because:
options: Tadpoles need water to live and breathe through gills
questions.explanation: Tadpoles live in water, and their gills work only in water.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which statement about a zygote is correct?
options: It has only the mother's genes
It is formed by fusion of a sperm and an egg and has genes from both parents
questions.explanation: The zygote gets genetic material from both gametes.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why does a child look like both parents?
questions.answer: The zygote is formed by fusion of a sperm from the father and an egg from the mother, so it gets genes from both. These genes decide the features of the child.
keyPoints: Zygote from father's sperm and mother's egg
questions.explanation: Features are passed on through genes.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Hormones are secreted by:
questions.explanation: Endocrine glands release hormones into the blood.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The stage when the body becomes capable of reproduction is called:
questions.explanation: Puberty is the stage when sexual maturity is reached.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The adrenal glands are located:
questions.explanation: The adrenal glands sit on top of the two kidneys.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is goitre and how can it be prevented?
questions.answer: Goitre is a swelling in the neck caused by a lack of iodine, which the thyroid gland needs to make thyroxine. It can be prevented by using iodised salt and eating iodine-rich food.
keyPoints: Swelling of the thyroid gland in the neck
questions.explanation: Iodine is needed by the thyroid gland.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A teenager develops pimples on the face. What is the best advice?
options: Wash the face regularly with clean water and avoid squeezing the pimples
questions.explanation: Oily skin at puberty causes pimples, and good hygiene helps.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: When a girl has her first menstrual period, it generally means that:
options: She has reached puberty and her body is maturing for reproduction
She has become an adult in all ways
questions.explanation: The first period is a sign of puberty in girls.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why should adolescents stay away from tobacco, alcohol and drugs?
questions.answer: These substances harm the body and the brain, especially during the growing years. They can become a habit that is hard to break and cause diseases and problems in studies and life.
questions.explanation: Healthy habits in adolescence matter a lot.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which example shows a force changing the shape of an object?
options: A ball rolling on the ground
questions.explanation: Squeezing makes the sponge change its shape.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Atmospheric pressure is measured with a:
questions.explanation: A barometer is used to measure air pressure.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The amount of friction between two surfaces depends on:
options: The shape of the object only
The roughness of the surfaces and the force pressing them together
questions.explanation: Rougher surfaces and a greater pressing force give more friction.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A lubricant reduces friction because it:
options: Forms a thin layer between the surfaces
Increases the force pressing on them
questions.explanation: Oil and grease keep the surfaces from rubbing directly.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is the difference between contact forces and non-contact forces? Give one example of each.
questions.answer: A contact force acts only when objects touch each other, such as muscular force or friction. A non-contact force acts without touching, such as gravity or the force of a magnet.
questions.explanation: Gravity is a non-contact force.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A car skids on a wet road because:
options: A film of water reduces the friction between the tyres and the road
questions.explanation: Water between the tyres and the road reduces friction.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A glass is filled with water and covered with a card. When it is turned upside down, the card stays in place because:
options: Atmospheric pressure pushes the card upward
questions.explanation: The upward push of the air on the card is more than the weight of the water.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Explain how the brakes of a bicycle stop it.
questions.answer: When the brake lever is pressed, the brake pads press against the rim of the wheel. The friction between the pads and the rim opposes the motion and slows the wheel until it stops.
keyPoints: Brake pads press on the wheel rim
questions.explanation: Brakes work by increasing friction.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Sound travels through air in the form of:
questions.explanation: Vibrations pass through air as sound waves.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following produces sound by a vibrating air column?
questions.explanation: In a flute the air inside the tube vibrates.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: An echo is:
options: A sound that is louder than normal
The sound that is heard after reflection from a surface
questions.explanation: An echo is the repetition of a sound after it bounces back from a surface.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The speed of sound in air is about:
questions.explanation: Sound travels at roughly 340 m/s in air at ordinary temperatures.
